comment: What each job and each of its named steps actually covers.
This exists because the answer used to be spread across a thousand lines of
YAML, and nothing compared two steps that named overlapping suites. A suite
listed twice for one platform is duplicate execution; a guarantee listed
nowhere is a guarantee no job is holding. `validate-ci-coverage.lua` checks
this file against the workflow and against tests/groups.lua on every run,
before anything expensive is provisioned, so it cannot go quietly stale.
`suites` and `groups` name what a step runs. `guarantees` name what it is
for, in the words the plan and the release notes use.

steps.name: Classify the affected surfaces
guarantees: every change selects the jobs that can observe it

steps.name: Validate selected-job aggregation
guarantees: a selected correctness job cannot pass by being skipped or absent

steps.name: Validate the workflow against the classifier
guarantees: the classifier, this map and the workflow name the same jobs

steps.name: Check the formatting
guarantees: committed source is what nupp fmt --write produces

steps.name: Check the compiler
guarantees: the compiler type-checks its own sources

steps.name: Run the shared-process suites
guarantees: every suite a Nupp worker can share a process with

steps.name: Verify the self-hosting fixpoint
guarantees: the compiler rebuilds itself byte-identically from stage zero

steps.name: Compile every homepage example in LuaJIT mode
guarantees: every homepage example compiles under the browser Worker's default settings

steps.name: Validate the LuaJIT browser compiler bundle
guarantees: the browser compiler answers the checked request corpus and fits its startup budget

steps.name: Regenerate and verify the documentation
guarantees: every diagnostic code has a reference section
every documented Nupp example checks, or is marked a fragment or a refused program
the LuaJIT playground checks and runs programs in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
real changing-source editor latency is recorded for both browser backends
the LuaJIT compiler and application runtime execute in the browser guest
browser applications and templates run in Chromium

steps.name: Require every selected job to have succeeded
guarantees: one stable status whose meaning survives job reorganization

steps.name: Record the run
guarantees: queue time, execution time, conclusion and revision are retained
